skill.name: audit-campaign-tracking
skill.description: Inspect supplied campaign links and plan a test for UTM tags and ad click identifiers. Use when traffic is unattributed or a user asks where source, medium, campaign, gclid, or yclid are lost.
skill.summary: Audit campaign links for missing or inconsistent tracking tags and plan a test to find where attribution is lost.
skill.author: qonvert-marketing-ai

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks format UTM parameter names in Markdown. The instruction checks query parameters in supplied links and does not invoke Ruby or a shell.
The backticks format ad click identifier names in Markdown. The line explains when platforms add identifiers and contains no executable command.
The URLs cite public Google Analytics and Yandex Metrica documentation. They contain no sample data and do not instruct the agent to transmit it.
The description limits inspection to supplied campaign links and calls for a tracking test plan. It does not request discovery of hosts, services, or system configuration.

content.user_title: Audit Campaign Links and Tracking Tags
content.value_statement: When campaign traffic appears without attribution, a sample link alone cannot show where tracking was lost. Check the link tags and plan a test at the earliest stage that lacks evidence.
actual_capabilities: Check supplied links for missing, empty, or duplicate UTM parameters and compare values with team naming rules.
Check optional UTM content and term tags when they are needed for reporting.
Distinguish ad click identifiers from UTM tags and explain why a sample link cannot verify click-time tagging.
Separate observations confirmed in a sample, observations confirmed by a test, and observations that need evidence.
Plan a tracking test across redirects, the landing page, and the relevant conversion record.
Summarize observations and next checks in a table and suggest a corrected link with synthetic tags when useful.
limitations: A sample without a click identifier cannot establish whether the ad platform attaches one during a real click.
Link inspection does not verify analytics events or downstream records without test evidence.
Naming checks require the team's agreed UTM conventions.
The workflow requires approval before opening links with sensitive values or editing live campaigns.

use_cases.title: Check Links Before a Launch
use_cases.description: Review launch links for missing, empty, or duplicate UTM tags and compare their values with campaign naming rules.

use_cases.title: Investigate Unattributed Paid Traffic
use_cases.description: Use redacted samples and report evidence to identify the first unverified step in paid traffic attribution.

use_cases.title: Trace Attribution to an Order
use_cases.description: Use event and order evidence to plan a test for the handoff where campaign attribution may be lost.

prompt_templates.title: Check One Link
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: review a redacted campaign link before sharing it.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this redacted campaign link without opening it: [link]. Check for missing, empty, or duplicate source, medium, and campaign tags. The channel is [channel] and the destination report is [report].

prompt_templates.title: Compare Tags Across Channels
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: compare samples against shared naming rules.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these redacted links from [channels] for [report]. Compare their UTM tags against [naming rules]. Return a table with sample labels, observations, implications, and next checks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Paid Click Test
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: a paid campaign sample has no click identifier.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this redacted paid campaign link and the available evidence for [report]. Separate what the sample confirms from what still needs testing. Plan an approved test using a provider-generated click identifier through redirects and the landing page.

prompt_templates.title: Trace a Conversion Across Systems
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: a conversion record has no campaign attribution.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review redacted evidence from the link, redirects, landing page, analytics event, and [CRM or order record]. Distinguish sample observations from test results. Identify the earliest unverified stage and propose the next check without making live changes.

output_examples.input: A redacted email link has source and campaign tags, but its medium tag is empty.
output: Confirmed in the sample: The medium tag is present but empty.
Implication: This link does not supply a medium value for reporting.
Next check: Verify the agreed email medium value before correcting the campaign link.

output_examples.input: An approved paid search test recorded a click identifier at the landing page, but the order has no campaign attribution.
output: Confirmed by a test: The click identifier reached the landing page.
Needs evidence: It is not clear whether the conversion event carried the identifier.
Next check: Inspect the redacted conversion event before investigating the order handoff.

best_practices: Provide labeled sample links with sensitive values removed, along with the originating channels and destination report.
Share your naming conventions so the audit can distinguish missing tags from inconsistent values.
Use an approved click with a provider-generated identifier and redact values when reporting test results.
anti_patterns: Do not assume live tracking is broken because a sample link has no click identifier.
Do not use an invented click identifier to validate live attribution.
Do not open links with sensitive values or edit live campaigns without approval.

faq.question: What should I provide for an audit?
faq.answer: Provide a few labeled links with sensitive values removed, their originating channels, and the destination report. Include your naming conventions when available.

faq.question: Which UTM tags does the audit check?
faq.answer: It checks source, medium, and campaign. It also checks content and term when your reporting uses them.

faq.question: Which ad click identifiers does it recognize?
faq.answer: It recognizes gclid, gbraid, wbraid, and yclid as ad click identifiers, not UTM tags.

faq.question: Does a missing click identifier mean tracking is broken?
faq.answer: No. Ad platforms can add identifiers at click time, so a sample link does not verify what happens during a live click.

faq.question: Can it tell where order attribution was lost?
faq.answer: It can identify the last stage supported by your evidence and recommend the next check. A sample link alone cannot confirm the cause.

faq.question: Will it open sensitive links or change campaigns?
faq.answer: The workflow calls for approval before opening links with sensitive values or editing live campaigns. A sample review can start with redacted links.
